correctness.rationale: Nonunital maps are excluded by explicit classification of possible F(1) and the one-dimensional Peirce-one space for primitive idempotents, which would imply an impossible rank-one character form when B has rank at least two. Unital maps are forced to have zero scalar functional and exactly orthogonal/rectangular/radical block normal form. Idempotency gives U^2=U, US=0; composition and conjugation show one orbit for every radical projection rank. Gaussian, GL and isometry counts yield the full rank polynomials. The reduced idempotent strata are vector bundles over connected smooth projection varieties of stated dimensions. Exact finite-field checks of the original product equations and independent radical projections succeed, including F3 m=2,r=1 and r=2. Characteristic and quotient-rank boundaries are explicit.

value.rationale: For a natural and previously studied family of degenerate Jordan algebras, the result completely identifies the endomorphism monoid and all algebra retracts, rather than a chosen parameter slice. Its exact full-rank and retraction polynomials, one conjugacy orbit per retraction rank, smooth geometric component dimensions and Witt-independence of retract counts are nontrivial natural invariants. The derived intermediate-rank concentration for large radicals explains how generic retracts differ from extremal ones. These are motivated mathematical classification and counting problems, not merely correctness of a small computation.
